description: Phase 0 retrieval-eval fixture: known prior alpha_engine experiments, failures, and findings with research-intent queries and relevance judgments. Grounds Phase 2 exit criteria (recall@k and failure-recall@k, k=10, target 0.8). Documents mirror real alpha_engine MCP tools (run_momentum_backtest, run_factor_analysis, run_backtest, attribute_portfolio, brinson_attribution, portfolio_risk_decomposition, risk_decompose, optimize_portfolio, causal_test, ml_signal_scores) and their tested parameter/metric names.

documents.title: Cross-sectional momentum 126d/top20 monthly backtest
documents.text: Cross-sectional momentum backtest over S&P 500 history: each month buy the top 20 tickers by trailing 126-day return, equal weight, 5 bps fees. Sharpe 0.82 vs 0.51 equal-weight benchmark, CAGR 13.2%, max drawdown -28.4%, one-way turnover 3.4x per year. Baseline 6-month momentum result net of modest costs.

documents.title: Short-horizon momentum 21d/top10 weekly backtest
documents.text: Short-horizon momentum backtest: top 10 tickers by trailing 21-day return, rebalanced weekly. Sharpe only 0.31 with very high one-way turnover of 18.7x per year, so net results are fragile to transaction cost assumptions. Companion to the 126-day monthly baseline.

documents.title: Long-horizon momentum 252d/top50 monthly backtest
documents.text: Long-horizon 12-month momentum backtest: top 50 tickers by trailing 252-day return, monthly rebalance. Sharpe 0.64 with low turnover 1.9x per year, so the result survives realistic costs. Broader, more diversified expression of the momentum premium.

documents.title: Factor tearsheet: mom_126d IC and quantile backtest
documents.text: Single-factor evaluation of the built-in mom_126d signal: Spearman IC mean 0.032, ICIR 0.71, t-stat 2.46, hit rate 0.56 over a 21-day horizon. Quintile long-short backtest earns Sharpe 0.68 with 2.9x turnover and 93% rebalance coverage. Includes IC decay by horizon and seasonality diagnostics.

documents.title: Factor tearsheet: value DSL expression, sector-neutral
documents.text: Custom value factor defined with the expression DSL as price over trailing 1-year moving average minus one, sector-neutralized. IC mean 0.018 at 63 days, long-short Sharpe 0.39, low turnover 1.4x. Demonstrates expression-defined signals with group neutralization.

documents.title: Factor tearsheet: rsi_14 and reversal_5d short-term reversal
documents.text: Short-term reversal study: rsi_14 has negative 21-day IC of -0.021 while the reversal_5d signal earns positive 5-day IC of 0.027 with long-short Sharpe 0.52, but at extreme 22.4x turnover that demands a careful cost model. Labels formed at date t earn returns from t+1 with no look-ahead.

documents.title: Factor tearsheet: vol_63d low-volatility effect
documents.text: Trailing 63-day volatility signal: negative IC mean of -0.014 means high-volatility names underperform forward, consistent with the low-volatility effect. Weak statistical strength (ICIR -0.38) so position sizing must stay modest.

documents.title: Momentum parameter sweep over lookback and top_n grid
documents.text: Grid sweep of cross-sectional momentum over lookback 21/63/126/189/252 days and top_n 10/20/30/50 on compiled numba kernels with CUDA screening. Best in-sample config is lookback 126 top 20 at Sharpe 0.82. Winner must be rerun in float64 and validated out of sample before any claim.

documents.title: Deterministic momentum backtest with costs and purge/embargo
documents.text: spark-mcp 15.2 deterministic cross-sectional momentum backtest: trailing 20-day signal, 5-day holding, point-in-time universe, 7 bps total daily cost drag with purge 5 and embargo 10 splits. Net Sharpe 0.61 over 1520 days, gross 0.94, cost drag 0.33 Sharpe points, OOS Sharpe 0.44. Signals strictly causal, labels only from days after the signal day.

documents.title: Deterministic short-term reversal backtest with costs
documents.text: spark-mcp 15.2 reversal backtest: negated trailing 5-day signal, 5-day holding, same cost and split discipline as the momentum leg. Net Sharpe 0.38, OOS 0.22, with fat tails (kurtosis 5.6). Reversal works at short horizons and fades as lookback and holding lengthen.

documents.title: FF5-plus-momentum attribution of a tech-tilted portfolio
documents.text: Factor attribution of a concentrated tech portfolio on Fama-French 5 factors plus momentum: market beta 1.18 with t-stat 24.3, negative size and value loadings, R-squared 0.91, annualized alpha 1.2% with insignificant t-stat 0.80, residual vol 6.2%. Returns are explained by factor exposures, not stock picking.

documents.title: Brinson sector attribution vs equal-weight benchmark
documents.text: Multi-period Brinson-Fachler attribution of a tech-overweight portfolio against an equal-weight S&P 500 benchmark. Per-period allocation 0.4%, selection 1.1%, interaction -0.2%, active total 1.3%, cumulative active return 8.6%. Selection within sectors dominates the sector allocation call.

documents.title: Portfolio risk decomposition with EWMA factor covariance
documents.text: Linear factor risk model decomposition with EWMA covariance at halflife 66 over a 756-day lookback: total vol 18.2%, common factor vol 14.1%, specific vol 11.5%. Portfolio carries positive momentum exposure 0.42 and negative volatility exposure. Factor returns come from per-date cross-sectional regressions on style exposures plus sector dummies.

documents.title: Risk decomposition with sample covariance and Newey-West lags
documents.text: Same four-name portfolio under a plain sample factor covariance with Newey-West Bartlett-kernel adjustment at 5 lags: total vol 17.6% vs 18.2% under EWMA. Shows how covariance method choice moves the common-vs-specific split; covariance is PSD-cleaned and annualized.

documents.title: Book factor exposures vs daily factor store (ff5+momentum)
documents.text: spark-mcp 15.2 book risk decomposition: holdings regressed on daily ff5 plus momentum factor returns over a trailing 3-year window. Market exposure 1.05, momentum 0.21, annualized specific risk 9.8%. Factor aliases resolve against marts.factors_daily daily rows.

documents.title: Max-Sharpe optimization with single-name cap
documents.text: PyPortfolioOpt maximum-Sharpe mean-variance optimization over 12 names with a 20% single-name cap. In-sample expected Sharpe 1.24 is overstated by estimation error in sample means; treat as an upper bound and shrink or constrain before trading. Companion HRP and Black-Litterman runs diversify better.

documents.title: Hierarchical Risk Parity allocation over the same names
documents.text: Hierarchical Risk Parity allocation via skfolio over the same 12 names: max weight 11%, expected vol 14.8%, no mean estimates required. HRP is the robust fallback when sample means are too noisy for mean-variance optimization.

documents.title: Black-Litterman tilt with an outright outperformance view
documents.text: Black-Litterman optimization from an equal-cap prior with a single view that AAPL outperforms: tilts AAPL up 4 percentage points with modest, stable weight changes elsewhere. Views default to historical means when unspecified.

documents.title: Pairwise Granger causality among mega-cap tech and energy
documents.text: Pairwise Granger-causality F-tests on real daily returns over a trailing 3-year window, lags 1 to 5. AAPL helps predict MSFT at p 0.003 while the reverse is insignificant at p 0.41; energy shows no lead-lag with tech. PCMCI methods are refused by this tool; Granger only.

documents.title: Walk-forward ridge blend of momentum, vol, and RSI signals
documents.text: Walk-forward ML composite: ridge regression fit only on data strictly before each monthly rebalance predicts 21-day forward returns from mom_126d, vol_63d, and rsi_14 with 504 training dates. Latest coefficients load positively on momentum 0.61 and negatively on volatility and RSI. Point-in-time with no look-ahead.

documents.title: Costs erase short-horizon momentum edge
documents.text: Failed experiment: weekly short-horizon momentum with 18.7x turnover goes from gross Sharpe 1.08 to net Sharpe -0.15 once 20 bps costs plus 5 bps slippage are charged. Lesson: any backtest without an explicit bps/slippage/borrow cost model and turnover report is not evidence of an edge.

documents.title: Survivorship bias from current-snapshot universe
documents.text: Failed experiment: momentum backtest run on current S&P 500 constituents instead of point-in-time membership overstated CAGR by 4.7 points (14.8% vs 10.1% PIT). Lesson: historical selection must use survivorship-bias-free membership intervals (universe_members_as_of), never the current snapshot.

documents.title: Naive day-equality join drops all monthly factor rows
documents.text: Failed analysis: joining month-end AQR/JKP factor rows to daily data on exact calendar day dropped nearly 100% of factor rows and silently produced an empty regression. Fixed by joining on month periods (date_trunc month) or asof, which recovers correlation 0.78 between jkp_be_me and ff_hml. Never naive-join cross-frequency data.

documents.title: Look-ahead bias: forward labels included the signal day
documents.text: Failed experiment: forward-return labels accidentally included the signal day t, inflating IC to 0.19; after enforcing the timing rule that labels formed at t earn returns only from t+1, IC fell to 0.024. Lesson: every factor and backtest must assert strictly causal alignment before trusting any metric.

documents.title: Mixed yfinance/Stooq prices corrupt returns with unadjusted closes
documents.text: Failed ingest: Stooq fallback rows carry source stooq with unadjusted adj_close, so a split event appeared as a 38% one-day return and poisoned momentum ranks and risk estimates. Lesson: check the per-row source flag and never mix adjusted and unadjusted closes in one return series.

documents.title: Calendar-window momentum diverges on gapped series
documents.text: Failed replication: reimplementing momentum with calendar-day windows instead of trailing trading-row windows changed ranks (rank correlation 0.91) and top-20 membership on gapped series. Lesson: momentum uses trailing trading-row windows by convention; the engine backtests remain authoritative on window semantics.

documents.title: Concurrent dbt build corrupts in-flight MCP reads
documents.text: Failed operations: running alpha-engine build and dbt while MCP queries were in flight hit the DuckDB single-writer rule and failed 14 reads. Lesson: Python read paths open read-only and the build is the sole writer; never run ingest or dbt while queries are in flight because reads only degrade gracefully.

documents.title: Sweep winner collapses out of sample
documents.text: Failed inference: the 20-config sweep winner (lookback 21, top 10) posted in-sample Sharpe 1.92 but only 0.08 out of sample. Lesson: grid mining overfits; always hold out an OOS window with purge and embargo splits and discount the best of many backtests before claiming a discovery.

documents.title: Brinson attribution fails with fewer than two shared rebalance dates

metrics.error: ValueError: need at least two shared rebalance dates

documents.text: Failed run: Brinson attribution raised ValueError because portfolio and benchmark shared only one rebalance date, so no return period exists. Lesson: periods run between consecutive shared rebalance dates; align both weight schedules to at least two common dates before attributing.

documents.title: IC collapses to NaN on thin cross-sections
documents.text: Failed analysis: running the factor tearsheet on a 20-name narrow universe left only 12% of dates with the minimum 5 names for a meaningful IC, so the IC series was mostly NaN. Lesson: check rebalance coverage and cross-sectional counts first; thin universes cannot support IC inference.

documents.title: PCMCI causal method refused; Granger required
documents.text: Failed run: requesting a pcmci-plus causal test raised ValueError because only Granger F-tests are supported. Lesson: the causal tool contract is Granger-only on daily returns with lags 1..5; plan lead-lag studies within that method and window.

documents.title: CUDA float32 screening ranks differ from float64 exact run
documents.text: Failed shortcut: trusting CUDA float32 screening ranks directly flipped 2 of the top 5 sweep configs versus the exact float64 rerun. Lesson: GPU screening is for triage only; always rerun the winner with exact precision before recording metrics.

documents.title: 6-12 month momentum earns positive IC net of 5 bps costs
documents.text: Validated finding: 6-12 month cross-sectional momentum on liquid US equities earns positive information coefficients of 0.02 to 0.035 and survives 5 bps transaction costs at monthly turnover. Supported by the 126-day and 252-day backtests and the mom_126d factor tearsheet; contradicted only when costs exceed 15 bps or universes are thin.

documents.title: Turnover above 10x per year erases short-horizon momentum
documents.text: Validated finding: short-horizon momentum strategies turning over more than 10x per year lose their entire edge once costs exceed about 10 bps per side. Supported by the weekly 21-day backtest and the cost-erasure failure; short-horizon signals must be evaluated net of explicit bps, slippage, and borrow.

documents.title: Cross-frequency factor joins must use month periods or asof
documents.text: Methodological finding: monthly factor rows such as AQR and JKP must be joined to daily data via month periods (date_trunc month) or asof, never naive calendar-day equality, which silently drops the factor leg. Month-period joins recover correlation 0.78 between jkp_be_me and ff_hml.

documents.title: EWMA halflife 66 balances responsiveness and stability for factor covariance
documents.text: Methodological finding: EWMA factor covariance with halflife 66 over a 756-day lookback balances responsiveness to regime change against estimation stability for US equity risk models. Sample covariance with Newey-West lags is the documented fallback when autocorrelation adjustment is required.
